title: "Local Variables and Scope"

# Local Variables and Scope

In Bash, all variables are global by default—even when defined inside a function. Always use `local` to prevent state contamination:

```bash
counter=100

my_function() {
    local counter=1 # Scoped exclusively to this function and its callees
    echo "Inside: $counter"
}

my_function
echo "Outside: $counter" # 100 (Unchanged)
```

*Dynamic Scoping Warning:* Bash uses dynamic scoping, not lexical scoping. A `local` variable declared in function `A` is visible to function `B` if `A` calls `B`!
